Bounded investigations

On this page
  1. Discover, then select
  2. Call-site context and reverse calls
  3. Limits and partial results

Available starting with v0.2.0. The JSON CLI and the local MCP xref_query tool accept the same request. The inspected file is read, never executed.

Discover, then select

JSON
{
  "operation": "investigate",
  "request": {
    "seed": {"kind": "text", "text": "invalid request"},
    "direction": "both",
    "limits": {"depth": 1, "functions": 8, "rows": 10}
  }
}

For a known entry range, use "seed":{"kind":"function","address":"0x1000"}. Addresses here illustrate request shapes, not an address valid in your image. Optional callee restricts returned call-site candidates to the FDE containing that address; it does not prune the graph traversal.

Discovery composes typed strings -> refs -> FDE candidates -> calls (and callers when requested). It returns every candidate admitted by the limits. Two instructions calling the same target remain two candidates. The evidence array records operation inputs, parent step IDs, typed results, pagination, warnings and per-step errors. string_matches records the exact matched byte range, not the bounds of an entire source string. ambiguities identifies multiple matches/functions/call sites. No pseudo-C or slice is generated during discovery.

Each call-site candidate carries a selection object with image_sha256, function and call_site. Copy the whole object into the next request:

JSON
{
  "operation": "investigate",
  "request": {
    "seed": {"kind": "function", "address": "0x1000"},
    "selection": {
      "image_sha256": "<digest returned by discovery>",
      "function": "0x1000",
      "call_site": "0x1011"
    }
  }
}

Use the same seed/traversal limits to reproduce the discovered scope, or narrow to its returned function. A selection from different image bytes is rejected. A selection not reached in this request is reported as selection_not_reached_under_limits; no alternative is silently substituted. Only an explicitly selected instruction triggers a slice. That slice reuses the CLI renderer with its exact instruction-address target. Its evidence step contains text pagination; follow up with the ordinary slice operation and returned byte offset to retrieve further fragments.

Call-site context and reverse calls

JSON
{"operation":"call_context","address":"0x1000","call_site":"0x1011"}

The result includes instruction bytes/addresses, reaching definitions for the six SysV integer argument-register candidates, and conditional edges necessary to reach the site under the direct CFG model. Guards include the branch and flag-definition instruction addresses; the result does not invent a source predicate. Raw evidence remains available through asm.

Register candidates are not a recovered signature or proof of callee arity. The conservative dataflow currently recognizes 32/64-bit immediate moves, 64-bit register copies, register-zeroing XOR and RIP-relative address-taking. Memory loads, unsupported arithmetic and partial-register updates become unknown. At joins, a value is retained only when every modeled incoming path agrees. Definitions are capped at eight per register. Calls clobber SysV volatile registers; continuation assumes a returning call. Unknown control-flow edges suppress recovered values and make the context incomplete; required guards are withheld when the CFG has unknown edges or the site is unreachable from the FDE entry. Valid trap instructions and resolved external tail jumps are modeled as terminating edges. Exception unwinding, computed jump targets, stack arguments, vector arguments and interprocedural return values are outside this model. An entry-register value denotes the entry of an FDE range, not necessarily the entry of a complete source function.

Contexts have at most 32 KiB code / 2048 instructions, 100000 dataflow work items, 200000 guard-search items, 16 guards and 96 evidence instructions. Budget/unknown-edge flags are explicit. Lists of definition addresses can outlive the capped inline instruction evidence; retrieve those through asm. A direct call_context query lets the caller inspect a candidate omitted by the compound context budget.

JSON
{"operation":"callers","address":"0x1100","page":{"limit":20}}

Reverse calls preserve each known call instruction and its caller FDE, including recognized tail jumps and pointer-resolved calls. Target matching uses the covering FDE; the original target address is retained. Unresolved indirect edges, missing unwind ranges and scan limits prevent a negative result from proving absence of a relationship.

Limits and partial results

Defaults: depth 1, eight functions, 24 primitive steps, ten rows per list, four call-site contexts, 32768 output bytes, 4096 slice bytes. Allowed maxima: depth 3, 16 functions, 32 steps, 20 rows, eight contexts, 48000 output bytes and 8192 slice bytes. Set contexts: 0 to skip automatic contexts during discovery. An explicitly selected site still requests its slice and context, in that order. Optional contexts follow selected work. Traversal is breadth first with FDE deduplication; cycles are not expanded repeatedly. Depth counts graph edges beyond every seed FDE. Even reverse-only traversal enumerates calls inside discovered FDEs as selectable candidates. The function limit caps queued FDE expansions; reverse-call rows retain their exact call sites even if their caller cannot be queued or its first call page omits that instruction. The independent context/step budgets still apply.

The compound request admits at most 100000 FDE ranges; text-seed reference scans additionally admit 64 MiB of summed FDE range bytes. A known function seed can traverse a local callee graph in a larger image without that whole-image reference scan. Reverse-call scans independently cap decoded code at 64 MiB and warn when ranges are skipped. These caps bound work; they do not measure wall-clock latency. The loaded image and base API budgets still apply. Results preserve admitted evidence when a step, function, row, context, depth or serialized-output limit is reached. Continuation is explicit follow-up queries or a narrowed investigation, rather than a hidden automatic scan. Cancellation is checked between stages and during core scans; rendering retains the existing between-phase cancellation behavior.

stops explains why the bounded request stopped. In particular, selection_required, not_found_under_limits, depth_limit and row_or_text_limit are not global claims about the binary. Inspect each step's warnings, errors and pagination. Known direct graph edges do not establish the absence of indirect calls or deferred work.

This interface supports collecting positive native evidence for a concrete entry-point question. It does not identify an unknown entry by business semantics, prove a field was forwarded because its base was forwarded, or conclude that deferred work is absent because no immediate call was found.
